name: Rifampin
executiveSummary: Potent inducing rifamycin. Adult TB: **10 mg/kg/day** (usual **600 mg** PO/IV). Staph synergy: **300–450 mg every 12 h** or **600 mg/day**. Meningococcal prophylaxis: **600 mg every 12 h × 2 days**.
indications:
## Indications

- Tuberculosis (always in combination).
- Prophylaxis of *N. meningitidis* / *H. influenzae* type b contacts.
- Synergy in prosthetic / staphylococcal osteomyelitis (never monotherapy).

## Precautions

- Hepatotoxicity — baseline LFTs; symptom education.
- **Potent CYP3A4/P-gp inducer** (anticoagulants, immunosuppressants, contraceptives, ARVs, etc.).
- Orange body fluids; stains soft contact lenses.
- IV: prefer D5W; short stability once diluted.

> Never alone against staph (rapid resistance).

adulto.dose: TB: **10 mg/kg/day** (usual max **600 mg**) PO or IV once daily. Staph synergy: **300 mg every 12 h** or **600 mg/day**. Meningococcal prophylaxis: **600 mg every 12 h × 2 days**. Hib prophylaxis: **600 mg/day × 4 days**.
adulto.administration: IV: reconstitute 10 mL SW; dilute in 100–500 mL D5W (preferred); infuse **30 min–3 h**. PO fasting if possible.
adulto.notes: May precipitate after ~4 h diluted. NS reduces stability.

pediatrico.presentation: Capsules/tablets 300 mg; syrup 20 mg/mL; vial 600 mg.
pediatrico.dose: TB: **10–20 mg/kg/day** every 24 h (max **600 mg**). <1 month: often **10 mg/kg/day**. Hib prophylaxis: neonate **10 mg/kg/day × 4 days**; child **20 mg/kg/day × 4 days**. Meningococcus: <1 month **10 mg/kg every 12 h × 2 days**; child **10 mg/kg every 12 h × 2 days** (max **600 mg**/dose). Synergy: **10–20 mg/kg/day** q12–24h (max **600 mg**).
pediatrico.notes: Caution/relative contraindication in significant liver disease.

neonatal.dose: Neonatal TB and prophylaxis per national/NNU protocol (often **10 mg/kg/day**).
neonatal.administration: PO preferred; IV if not tolerated.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted: ~24 h room temp.
- Diluted: ~4 h room temp — prepare close to administration.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, hepatitis/jaundice, flu-like syndrome (interrupted therapy), rash, thrombocytopenia, orange fluid discoloration.
